## Context / Problem
LLM failure classification is duplicated in one place and only one: the context-length phrase
list is byte-identical in `src/rebar/llm/failure.py:148-157` and
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:316-329`, and the comment at `failure.py:144-147` records
why the copy was made ("kept local so this low-level boundary module has no dependency on the
plan_review package — the two must stay in sync"). A fix to one silently leaves the other
stale, which is exactly the instalment pattern the fortnight review found.

Two adjacent duplications named in the original plan do NOT survive inspection and are
therefore out of scope:

* The stop-reason map is not a copy. `structured._BAD_STOP_REASONS` (`structured.py:616-627`)
  is keyed by finish/stop reason (`refusal`/`max_tokens`/`length`/`content_filter`/`error`) and
  its values are the EXCEPTION text raised at `structured.py:646,648,676`;
  `failure.message_for` (`failure.py:355`) is keyed by the disjoint 8-member `ResolutionClass`
  vocabulary and returns operator remedy prose. The key spaces share no member, so
  `message_for("refusal")` evaluates to `None` and `check_stop_reason` would raise with no
  message at all. Bug `injurious-definable-badger` (closed, landed `0e41876787` via Gerrit
  1525) already decided this deliberately: "Leave `check_response`'s raise text unchanged
  (already accurate)."
* The exit-code mapping is already centralised. `_cli/_llm_commands.py:45`
  `_llm_error_exit_code` and `:64-100` `_disposition_exit_code` are the two shared helpers;
  three verbs call them (`:147`, `:157`, `:231`, `:336`), plus `_commands/claim.py:120-123` and
  `_commands/composer.py:778-781` outside the file. There is no fourth hand-rolled copy to
  collapse, and the two remaining non-users diverge ON PURPOSE (see Deliberate divergences).

Bug `injurious-definable-badger` hid at the seam where one caller composed `message_for(...)`
without the `finish_reason`; all three render sites now thread it
(`_llm_commands.py:53-57,74-78`, `close_precheck.py:700-705`), so that seam is closed.

## Approach
**Scope reduction — read this first.** This story's genuine content is ONE duplication: the
eight-phrase `_CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS` tuple, copied byte-for-byte into `sizing.py`. The other three
consolidations the original plan proposed are WITHDRAWN, not deferred: the exit-code mapping is
already centralised (already done), the `structured.py` message merge is actively harmful and
was decided against in a closed merged bug, and the MCP payload helper composes no exit code at
all. What remains is a one-line import change plus its uniqueness guard.

`sizing.is_context_limit_error` stops carrying its own phrase tuple and reads
`failure._CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS` instead. The `def is_context_limit_error` STAYS in `sizing.py` —
`orchestrator.py:72` binds `_is_context_limit_error = sizing.is_context_limit_error` at import
time and `test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:45` monkeypatches the name as a string,
so a re-export in its place would desynchronise both. The import direction is
`sizing → failure`, which introduces no cycle (`failure.py` imports only `rebar.llm.errors`,
while `sizing.py:26-32` already imports `rebar.llm.config`, `.errors`, `.model_classes`,
`.runner`) and preserves the boundary-module constraint the `failure.py:144` comment records.

Guard: the eight-phrase CONJUNCTION appears in exactly one file. Match on the co-occurrence of
all eight literals within a single expression (per the epic's rule 2 — never on a single common
token such as `"context"`), exempt the owner `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, and honour a
`# context-hints-ok: <reason>` line marker.

### Deliberate divergences this story must NOT collapse
* `workflow/completion_failures.py:46-79` `_is_token_exhaustion` is a THIRD, intentionally
  different classifier: it omits the bare `"context"` substring the other two carry ("without
  mistaking generic context text") and additionally keys off a normalized `finish_reason` set
  (`:52-60`). Folding it in would make any message containing the word "context" read as token
  exhaustion.
* `_llm_commands.py:188-190` (`scan-spec`) returns a flat exit **1** on `LLMError`, and its MCP
  twin `_mcp_llm.py:109-133` has no `except` at all. Neither joins the disposition mapping.
* `_llm_commands.py:244-246` (`verify-completion`) carries an extra rule from bug 2a6f
  (`verdict_obtainable is False → 11`) and has no INDETERMINATE→2 arm.
* `close_precheck.py:691-714` additionally calls `failure.log_degrade` and
  `failure.close_gate_remedy`, and embeds the message in a `CommandError` rather than writing
  `llm-degrade: …` to stderr as the CLI helpers do.
* `_disposition_exit_code` reads `result["verdict"]` (accepting both the plan-review string and
  the nested code-review dict) and calls
  `plan_review.resign.classify_plan_review_attestation`; neither is reachable from an
  `LLMOutcome` nor from a `coverage` dict, so no `exit_code_for(outcome_or_coverage)` can
  replace it.

## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`: owner module exempt, match the constituent conjunction or AST shape named in Approach (or the definition count where no distinctive atom exists), `# <construct>-ok: <reason>` escape marker, and behaviour pinned only by the named existing tests.

## Scope
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` (drop the local tuple, import the owner's),
`src/rebar/llm/failure.py` (comment update only — the tuple is already correct),
`tests/unit/test_context_hints_single_source.py` (new; flat under `tests/unit/`, since
`tests/unit/llm/` does not exist).

Explicitly OUT of scope, with the reasons above: `src/rebar/llm/structured.py`,
`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py`,
`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py`.

## Testing
Guard: the eight-phrase conjunction resolves to exactly one file under `src/rebar` with the
owner exempt; the guard is proven to FLAG by reintroducing a second copy in a temp fixture, not
merely to pass.

Namesake survival: the guard leaves untouched `run_failure.py:190-191` and `enrich.py:47`
(docstrings quoting the phrases as prose), and `completion_failures.py:56,59,73` (the distinct
token-exhaustion classifier).

Pinning — must pass with no assertion edits: `tests/unit/test_llm_failure_classifier.py`
(`:188-211` asserts both classifiers agree on a wrapped context error and disagree on a
refusal), `tests/unit/test_change_input_not_an_outage_43d4.py::test_the_new_prefix_does_not_itself_look_like_a_context_limit`
(`:245-266`, the prefix-wording trap — the sharpest guard on this exact tuple),
`tests/unit/test_plan_review.py::test_is_context_limit_error_and_ladder` (`:1331`, reaches the
predicate through the import-time alias `orchestrator._is_context_limit_error`),
`tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py` (`:45`, monkeypatches
`sizing.is_context_limit_error` by string — the `def` must survive in `sizing.py`),
`tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The eight-phrase context-length list has exactly one definition under `src/rebar`;
      checked by `grep -rln 'too many tokens' src/rebar` returning exactly
      `src/rebar/llm/failure.py`, and by the new guard test.
- [ ] `sizing.is_context_limit_error` still exists as a `def` in
      `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` and reads the owner's tuple; checked by
      `grep -c 'def is_context_limit_error' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` returning `1`
      and `grep -n '_CONTEXT_LEN_HINTS' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` returning a hit.
- [ ] The three legitimate namesakes survive; checked by
      `grep -rln 'token limit' src/rebar` returning exactly `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` and
      `src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py`, and by
      `grep -c 'context_length_exceeded' src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py`
      returning `3`.
- [ ] `workflow/completion_failures.py::_is_token_exhaustion` is unchanged; checked by
      `git diff origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py` being empty.
- [ ] No exit-code or message behaviour changes; checked by
      `git diff origin/main -- src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py
      src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py src/rebar/llm/structured.py` being empty.
- [ ] The guard FAILS when a second copy is introduced, not just passes on a clean tree;
      checked by the guard test's own negative case.
- [ ] Pinning suites pass with no assertion edits; checked by
      `pytest tests/unit/test_llm_failure_classifier.py tests/unit/test_llm_failure_matrix.py
      tests/unit/test_change_input_not_an_outage_43d4.py tests/unit/test_plan_review.py
      tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py` and by
      `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` showing only additions.
- [ ] Net non-test line count is negative (the epic's consolidation guarantee); checked by
      `git show --numstat` on this story's trailer commit, excluding `tests/`.

## Review remediation (2026-08-21)
- The prior AC#1 grep was vacuous: `"maximum context length"` appears in NEITHER owner file — its only hit under `src/rebar` is `workflow/completion_failures.py:78`, so the criterion passed on unmodified `main` and would still name that file after a correct implementation.
- `workflow/completion_failures.py:46-79` holds a THIRD, deliberately different context classifier that omits the bare `"context"` substring and keys off a normalized `finish_reason` set; a hint-string uniqueness guard would demand deleting it, so it is exempted by name.
- The retryable→exit-code mapping was already centralised in two helpers (`_llm_commands.py:45` and `:64-100`) called by three verbs plus `claim.py:120-123` and `composer.py:778-781` — not four hand-rolled copies, so there was nothing left to collapse.
- `scan-spec` (`_llm_commands.py:188-190`, flat exit 1; MCP twin `_mcp_llm.py:109-133` has no `except`) and `verify-completion` (`_llm_commands.py:244-246`, the `verdict_obtainable is False → 11` rule from bug 2a6f, no INDETERMINATE→2 arm) opt out on purpose; a shared mapping would silently change both.
- `_disposition_exit_code` structurally needs `result["verdict"]` and `plan_review.resign.classify_plan_review_attestation`, neither of which is reachable from an `LLMOutcome` or a `coverage` dict, so the proposed `exit_code_for(outcome_or_coverage)` signature could not have replaced it.
- `structured._BAD_STOP_REASONS` (keyed by finish/stop reason, values are exception text) and `failure.message_for` (keyed by `ResolutionClass`, values are operator remedy prose) have disjoint key spaces — `message_for("refusal")` is `None` — and the merge was already decided against in `injurious-definable-badger` (closed, landed `0e41876787` via Gerrit 1525: "Leave `check_response`'s raise text unchanged").
